title: viewport-aware-grid-respacing-for-cost-insights-and-rollout-panels
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a resilient responsive strategy for the Cost Insights and Rollouts pages that prioritizes readable charts, stable table layouts, and non-overlapping modals across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox. Work includes a prototype of an adaptive grid that dynamically respaces cards and table columns, a 'graceful collapse' mode for chart canvases at small widths, and a z-index healing system to avoid modal and tooltip clipping when nested within portalled containers.

Background: Multiple teams have observed layout regressions when the Console is used on narrow viewports or when browser-specific rendering (Safari smooth-scrolling, Firefox subpixel rounding) triggers content shifts. This ticket captures the design deliverables and acceptance criteria for a cross-browser responsive polish that reduces visual breakage and improves perceived performance while preserving density for power users.

Scope:
- Cost Insights dashboard: adaptive card spacing, min-card widths, prioritized reflow order, and compact density toggle.
- Rollouts / feature flags panel: stable table column pinning on shrink, soft-wrapping rules for long labels, and compact action menus.
- Modals & overlays: anchor-aware stacking, shadow/edge-preservation rules, and keyboard focus management when a modal docks to the right on narrow screens.
- Charts: canvas fallback when WebGL or 2D subpixel rounding causes jitter; chart controls collapse into an overflow menu at <= 480px.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype with three viewport breakpoints (1200, 800, 420) showing reflow animations and density toggle states.
- Interaction spec (Confluence) describing stacking contexts, z-index policy, and scrolling anchor rules for Safari/Firefox.
- Usability test script + recordings for 8 participants across Mac/Windows.
- Implementation checklist for front-end engineers including CSS patterns (containment, transform-less affix, clamp() usage) and recommended polyfills.
acceptance_criteria: At 1200px the dashboard shows up to 4 cards per row with even gutters and preserved chart aspect ratios
At 800px cards respaced to 2 columns with controlled truncation for titles and actions moved into overflow
At 420px charts switch to the compact canvas mode with collapsed controls and no horizontal scroll
Modals opened within portalled containers remain fully visible and keyboard focus is trapped; ESC closes in all tested browsers
No layout jank > 50ms reported in Lighthouse CLS delta during 90s manual walkthroughs on Safari and Firefox

notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Aggressive truncation vs. preserving action visibility — chose contextual overflow to keep discoverability. 2) Heavy JS-driven layout vs. CSS-first approach — prioritized CSS clamp() and containment for perf; JS only to toggle density and complex anchoring. 3) Canvas vs. SVG for charts — canvas selected for compact mode to reduce DOM nodes and avoid SVG text wrapping inconsistencies across browsers.
